definitions.IsCompleteOn: def IsCompleteOn (a : ℕ → ℕ) (I : Set ℕ) : Prop := ∀ᶠ t in atTop, t ∈ subsetSums a I
definitions.IsDeletionMinimal: def IsDeletionMinimal (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := ∀ D : Set ℕ, D.Infinite → ¬ IsCompleteOn a Dᶜ
definitions.IsMinimalStablyComplete: def IsMinimalStablyComplete (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := StrictMono a ∧ (∀ n, 0 < a n) ∧ IsStablyComplete a ∧ IsDeletionMinimal a
definitions.IsStablyComplete: def IsStablyComplete (a : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop := ∀ D : Set ℕ, D.Finite → IsCompleteOn a Dᶜ
definitions.subsetSums: def subsetSums (a : ℕ → ℕ) (I : Set ℕ) : Set ℕ := {t | ∃ F : Finset ℕ, ↑F ⊆ I ∧ ∑ i ∈ F, a i = t}

literature_lock.verbatim_problem_core_en: Let A={1≤a1<a2<⋯} be a set of integers such that A\B is complete for any finite subset B and A\B is not complete for any infinite subset B. (Here 'complete' means all sufficiently large integers can be written as a sum of distinct members of the sequence.) Is it true that if a_{n+1}/a_n ≥ 1+ε for some ε>0 and all n then lim_n a_{n+1}/a_n = (1+√5)/2?
literature_lock.verbatim_question_en: Must ratios of consecutive terms in the specified minimal stably complete sequences converge to the golden ratio?

statement.Jsp288Claim: def Jsp288Claim : Prop := ∀ a : ℕ → ℕ, IsMinimalStablyComplete a → (∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ n, 1 + ε ≤ (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)) → Tendsto (fun n => (a (n + 1) : ℝ) / (a n : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 goldenRatio)
